evidence.claim: National LTC administration now uses a unified process, unified forms and a unified information subsystem covering disability assessment, service provision and reimbursement/settlement. This is direct evidence of reusable process and interface standardization, not evidence that a private orchestrator owns the process.

A signed Huaian LTC administration contract enumerates a bounded recurring scope: disability assessment, designated-provider agreement management, expense-detail preliminary review, audit, policy communication, training, consultation, complaint handling and fund monitoring.

Jiangsu explicitly describes a government-led, commercial-insurer-administered, care-institution-delivered LTC model; administration includes assessment, expense review, settlement, audit, service planning and quality tracking.

Xuzhou reports a designated LTC network spanning medical-nursing institutions, eldercare institutions, home-service institutions, assessment institutions and assistive-device institutions serving insured beneficiaries. Designation does not prove spare capacity.

The nationally unified LTC workflow repeatedly processes disability assessment, care-service provision and reimbursement/settlement events; these are intrinsic lifecycle events of continuing LTC administration rather than unrelated founder-led lead generation.

Xuzhou describes recurring benefit applications, home disability assessments and repeated home-care visits. Each visit uses location check-in and uploads service-process records to the LTC management platform.

Huaian published a signed 2026 renewal contract for LTC administration services with China Life Huaian branch. The contract total is CNY 6,620,303.03 for a nine-month performance period. This proves an accepted contracted payment basis, not settlement/payment completion.

Changzhou published a signed 2025 LTC service contract with Ping An Property & Casualty Jiangsu branch for CNY 22,440,000 and a one-year performance period. This is a second independent accepted payment basis for the LTC administration/service class, not proof of final settlement.

Xuzhou reports disability-assessment time falling from 60 days to 20 working days after third-party assessment cooperation, with intelligent-system use further improving review efficiency and a fastest reported benefit assessment of five working days. This is direct process-leverage evidence, but it does not isolate accumulated historical data, templates or rules as the cause of progressively better later cases.

Suzhou reports an LTC information system spanning application, assessment, admission, settlement and assessment/monitoring, with anomaly analysis and negative-list feedback used to improve supervision. The source does not provide a longitudinal before/after measure showing that accumulated history makes later routing or administration progressively cheaper, faster or more reliable.
